chapter_theme: Holy water (தீர்த்தம்): the true sacred waters are within the heart, where the Lord already dwells, and those of deceitful mind who wander from river to tank to wash away their deeds are seeking in a pond what they lost in the sea.
structure_note: Inner bathing against outer pilgrimage (509 to 511, 513), with one verse (512) that keeps the gods' bathing in the Ganga and one obscure verse (514) on the water within the body.

509.reading: There are many holy waters within the heart; those unlearned ones with deceitful minds who do not slowly plunge into them and bathe so that their deeds are destroyed wander over hollow and height.
509.nuance: பள்ளமும் மேடும் (hollow and height) is the pilgrim's road over the land. கல்வியிலோர் (the unlearned) is pointed: learning here means knowing where the waters are.

510.reading: To those who know the temple he appears gentle; those who know only bathing cannot join him; to those who know the breath he may or may not come; he is within the minds of those whose knowledge is clear.
510.nuance: The verse rings on four words: தளி (temple), குளி (bathing), வளி (breath, yoga) and தெளி (clarity). It ranks them, with bathing lowest and clear knowledge highest; வாய்க்கினும் வாய்க்கும் leaves the yogi's success open.

511.reading: None of the deceitful, however they mingle, know the One who is felt within the heart; those who seek out the flood of the river leave their evil deeds like something cast into a pit.
511.nuance: The last line (பள்ளத்தல் இட்டதோர் பத்துள்ளாமே) is obscure. It may mean that river bathing only sinks the deeds where they stay, or that the deeds cling like a பற்று (attachment, read for பத்து).

512.reading: The gods who know the First Lord go round the dense abode where he dwells, and plunging into the speckled water of the Ganga that flows on him who holds a deer and a bangled hand, they become meritorious.
512.nuance: This verse seems to grant outer bathing its place, for the gods and at the Lord's own river. மறியார் வளைக்கை may be the deer in the Lord's hand and the bangled hand of Uma beside him; பொறியார் புனல் is unclear. Some read the Ganga here as an inner current, which would bring the verse in line with the chapter.

513.reading: Losing it in the sea and looking for it in a pond: none match those who search by tiring the body; they do not know at all that by firm Nandi's grace he went and entered the body.
513.nuance: Line 1 is a proverb for searching in the wrong place. உடலுற்றுத் தேடுவார (variant உடலுற) may mean those who search with bodily toil, that is, by pilgrimage. The answer is that the Lord is already in the body.

514.reading: The water mixed in the body turns black, turns red, turns white; what mixed is water, fire and wind.
514.nuance: The three colours are not explained. They may be the body's three humours (wind, bile and phlegm) or three stages of a yogic practice; the plain point may only be that the body is itself made of the elements the pilgrim seeks outside.

links.note: The Kural's many who bathe with an air of distinction while their minds are stained, and Tirumular's deceitful who tramp from water to water: both deny that outer washing reaches the stain within.
116 says Nandi has made his home in the temple called this body; 513 draws the consequence for pilgrims, who search outside for one already inside.
510 says bathers alone cannot join the Lord; 512 lets the gods become meritorious by bathing in the Ganga. Bathing gains merit but not union, if the two are read together.

Kural 298 says 'புறந்தூய்மை நீரான் அமையும்', outer purity comes by water, and inner purity is seen by truthfulness. Tirumanthiram 509 says there are many holy waters 'உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளே', within the heart, and that those of deceitful mind who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height. Both deny that outer water cleans the inner person; the Tirumanthiram keeps the figure of bathing and moves the water inside.

Kural 294 says that one who does not lie 'உள்ளத்தால்', in his heart, dwells 'உள்ளத்துள் எல்லாம்', in the hearts of all the world. Tirumanthiram 511 says that the One felt 'உள்ளத்தின் உள்ளே', within the heart, is known by none of the 'கள்ளத்தினார்', the deceitful. Both make the heart the place of presence and make truth or deceit of heart the condition; the Kural speaks of a man's place among people, the Tirumanthiram of the Lord's place in a man.

source_issues: 511 line 4 (பள்ளத்தல் இட்டதோர் பத்துள்ளாமே) is obscure and may be corrupt.
513 line 1 ends with a stray full stop.
